### Fallback chain, part 1/7: A used-up Claude subscription window moves Claude model jobs to their tier's fallback instead of holding them (planned 2026-10-16 by user; design in plans/fallback-chain.md "What happens when a window is used up"; touches src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts src/gates/gate-polls.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/events/ docs/backends.md and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** Today a `rejected` claude.ai usage window (5-hour or weekly, with no extra usage) places a `claude` hold until `resetsAt`.

- Every subscription Claude model job waits for the reset. For the weekly window that can be days.
- With review on and a Claude reviewer, `reviewHeld` stops every role, including roles on pi.
- A configured `fallback` is used only at the daily cap or after three provider failures in a row, so it never helps here.

This part makes a used-up window a reason to move. While a window is rejected, each tier whose model job runs on subscription Claude runs on its tier's resolved free fallback (today's single fallback, `resolveTierFallbacks`), and returns when the window resets. With no fallback configured, nothing changes.

**Approach.**
- Add `claudeWindowUsedUp(account, now): { type: string; resetsAt: number } | null` to src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts.
  - It returns the subscription account's window with status `rejected`, no `isUsingOverage`, and a `resetsAt` still in the future. Among several, it returns the one with the latest `resetsAt`.
  - That is exactly the rule `claudeWindowObservation` (src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts) holds on today. Make `claudeWindowObservation` call it, so the hold and the move cannot disagree.
- `pollBudgetGate` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts) already reads the account each poll. Compute `windowOut = claudeWindowUsedUp(account, now)`, then:
  - **Fallback choice.** While `windowOut` is set, a subscription Claude pair is not a usable fallback: `pairFreeAt` refuses it. The resolution then falls through to the next tier's pair or pauses, exactly as it does for an unpriced pair.
  - **When to derive the view.** Derive the role view when `reached || windowOut`; today it is derived only when `reached`.
  - **Which jobs move.** The keep predicate passed to `applyFallbackModel` becomes "this model job's own model is available". While `windowOut` is set, no subscription Claude job is available. When `reached` is true, a job must also be free (`seamFree`, today's predicate). So below the cap a priced pi job keeps its primary, and only subscription Claude jobs move.
  - **Cache.** Re-derive the cached view (`state.from`) when `windowOut` changes, as well as when the live config changes.
  - **Return value.** Return `windowOut`, and the tiers it moved (`tierFallbackLabels` over the moved tiers), beside `gate`. `gate` keeps meaning the cap.
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts: the per-runner assignment already installs `roleConfig`. Keep `r.budgetFallbackActive` as the cap's flag: a window move below the cap does not restrict image reroute targets.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts: `reviewHeld` and `reviewHeldNow` read `seamHoldKey(reviewRunConfig(liveConfig))`. Read the reviewer's provider from the config merges actually review under, which is the derived `roleConfig` the poll returned. Otherwise a reviewer that has moved off Claude still holds the whole team on the `claude` hold.
- Leave the `claude` hold as it is. It still stops whatever still routes to subscription Claude: a tier with no usable fallback, and the director.
- **Return on reset.** On the poll where `windowOut` goes from set to null, hand back the in-flight non-director runs on the fallback pairs the window move used.
  - Do it the way gate-polls.ts's `gateResumed` branch does for the cap: one `budget_handback` event per pair, with a new optional `reason: "window"` field, then `r.handBackTick()`.
  - A window that resets while the team is over the cap hands back nothing, because the cap still holds.
- **Events.** `claude_window_limited` (src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts) gains an optional `tiers` field naming where each moved tier's work went, passed in from the budget poll. src/events/event-format.ts renders it the way it renders `budget_fallback`'s `tiers`, and renders `budget_handback`'s `reason`.
- The rejected run keeps its worktree as today (src/tick/tick-verdict.ts window arm). Its next run is on another backend, and src/tick/tick-resume.ts already turns that into a `handoff` resume. Nothing changes there; pin it with a test.
- docs/backends.md: the paragraph on rejected windows says the work moves to the tier's fallback and returns at the reset, and with no fallback it waits.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts.
- Docs: docs/backends.md.
- Tests: test/claude-account.test.ts, test/fleet-polls.test.ts, test/budget-gates.test.ts, test/event-format-fleet.test.ts, and test/gate-polls.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `claudeWindowUsedUp`:
  - A rejected window with a future `resetsAt` is returned.
  - Overage, API billing, a past `resetsAt`, and an `allowed_warning` window all return null.
  - Of two rejected windows, the later reset is returned.
  - `claudeWindowObservation`'s existing tests pass unchanged.
- `pollBudgetGate`, with `agent: "claude"`, a `fallback` naming a zero-priced pi pair, and spend under the cap:
  - With a rejected `five_hour` window, `roleConfig` resolves every role, the reviewer and the resolver to the fallback pair, and `gate` is `open`.
  - Without the rejected window, `roleConfig` is the live config object.
  - A priced pi role beside the Claude roles keeps its primary below the cap.
  - With no fallback configured, `roleConfig` is the live config, so today's hold applies.
- Wiring test (landed as test/gate-polls.test.ts's `pollFleetGates` seam over a fake runner, not a fake-claude/fake-pi orchestrator run; the `reviewHeld` key is the extracted `reviewHoldKey(roleConfig)` in src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, tested in test/budget-gates.test.ts against a poll's roleConfig; a cap reopen while the window is still used up hands nothing back, tested in test/gate-polls.test.ts):
  - After a rejected run, the roles' next runs start on the fallback, with the fallback pair's `--provider`, and `claude_window_limited` is logged once with `tiers`.
  - With review on and the reviewer on Claude, merges review on the fallback and `reviewHeld` blocks no role.
  - After `resetsAt` passes, an in-flight fallback run is handed back (`budget_handback` with `reason: "window"`), and the next run starts on Claude.
- The rejected run's next run is a `handoff` over the kept worktree.
- Every existing budget, hold and window test passes, and `npm test` passes.

**Landed notes.** A role pinned to subscription claude under a tier whose own model is not claude keeps its pin during a window (src/gates/budget-gates.ts), because dropping the pin would land it on the tier's priced primary; the `claude` hold still stops it. A reviewer pinned to subscription claude under such a tier goes to that tier's fallback pair instead, so the review does not hold the team. `claude_window_limited.tiers` names only tiers whose own model is claude.

### docs/cli.md gets a TUI keys table naming every Ctrl key the TUI handles, and a test keeps the two key sets equal (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry. It appends one section to docs/cli.md and adds only test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts. No source edits: it reads src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts and does not change it) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** README.md says "Every command, flag, and TUI key is in docs/cli.md", but cli.md mentions TUI keys only in passing inside command rows. A prototype scan on 2026-10-16 found these Ctrl keys handled in code: A B C D E F G L N O P Q R S T W X, plus the line-editing keys U and K. docs/cli.md names only A C E F N P Q W X. docs/how-it-works.md never names Ctrl+B (daily cap), Ctrl+C (interrupt the director), or Ctrl+D (quit). Add one reference table and a test that fails when a handler is added or removed without the table changing too.

**Approach.**
1. docs/cli.md: append a final section `## TUI keys` after the closing completion paragraph. Give it one sentence ("The hint line at the bottom of the TUI names the keys the current view takes."), then a `| Key | Where | What it does |` table with these rows. The wording comes from the hint labels in `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts` and the TUI paragraphs of docs/how-it-works.md:
   - `Ctrl+T` | any view | next view (Activity, each role's Transcript, Backlog, Usage, Failures, History, Pending, Inbox, Health, Brief); it also leaves an open editor
   - `Ctrl+D` | any view | quit the TUI (under `tumwater start --tui` this stops the team like Ctrl+C in the shell)
   - `Ctrl+C` | any view | interrupt the director's in-flight run, as `tumwater abort --role director` does; a notice when none is in flight
   - `Enter`, `↑`/`↓`, `PgUp`/`PgDn`, `Esc` | prompt line, panes | send the prompt, prompt history (or move through entries on Backlog), scroll, cancel an editor
   - `Ctrl+U` / `Ctrl+K` | prompt line | delete to the start / to the end of the line
   - `Ctrl+L` | prompt line | send later: set a delay for the next prompt
   - `Ctrl+B` | Activity | edit the daily cost cap (empty means no cap)
   - `Ctrl+F` | Activity | pause the team (`[duration] [reason]`), or resume it when paused
   - `Ctrl+Q` | Activity | stop the team later (a duration), or cancel a scheduled stop
   - `Ctrl+G` | Activity, History, Usage, Failures | cycle the role scope
   - `/` | Activity, History | search
   - `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+O` | History | cycle the trailing window / the outcome filter
   - `Ctrl+N` | History | the newest completed run's event trail, and back
   - `Ctrl+E` | Usage, Failures | cycle the trailing window
   - `Ctrl+R` | Transcript | send a prompt to that role
   - `Ctrl+P` / `Ctrl+W` / `Ctrl+A` | Transcript | pause or resume the role / wake it (a duration schedules it, `cancel` drops scheduled wakes) / stop its in-flight run
   - `Ctrl+N` | Transcript | cycle transcript, notes, and pending change; `Ctrl+X` pressed twice on notes clears them
   - `Ctrl+X` (twice) / `Ctrl+E` / `Ctrl+N` / `Ctrl+A` | Backlog | cancel the selected entry / edit its title / file a new plan or bug / answer the selected question
   - `Ctrl+E` / `Ctrl+X` | Inbox | edit / cancel the selected queued prompt
   Before writing each row, check its meaning against the handler in src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts or src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts. If a handler differs from the meaning above, write what the code does.
2. test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts (new; modeled on test/cli-doc.test.ts, reading sources with `fs.readFileSync` and `fileURLToPath(new URL("../../…", import.meta.url))`). Add a helper `handledCtrlKeys(): Set<string>` that returns upper-case letters:
   - In src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts, for every line containing `key.ctrl &&`, collect each `/key\.name === "([a-z])"/g` match. This covers the multi-name lines such as `key.ctrl && (key.name === "p" || key.name === "w")`.
   - In src/ui/tui/tui-input.ts, collect `/case "([a-z])":\s*(?:\/\/[^\n]*\s*)*if \(key\.ctrl\)/g` (yields `u` and `k`).
   Add a helper `documentedCtrlKeys(): Set<string>` that returns the `/Ctrl\+([A-Z])\b/g` letters in docs/cli.md from the `## TUI keys` heading to the next `## ` heading or the end of the file. Add three tests:
   - "the code scan finds the TUI's Ctrl keys": the handled set's size is at least 19, and it contains `D`, `T`, `U`. This floor stops a regex regression from passing vacuously.
   - "docs/cli.md's TUI keys table names every Ctrl key the TUI handles": `assert.deepEqual` of the sorted handled letters that are missing from the documented set against `[]`.
   - "docs/cli.md's TUI keys table names no Ctrl key the TUI lacks": the same check in reverse.
   Give the file a doc comment saying it compares the cli.md TUI keys table against the key handlers, tests only.

**Files touched.** docs/cli.md, test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With only the test file added (before the doc edit), the second test fails and names B C D G L O R S T U K. Check this before editing the doc; if the set differs, fix the scan or the plan's key list to match the code, not the reverse.
- On the tree as it lands, all three tests pass.
- Temporarily adding a `Ctrl+Z` row to the table makes the third test fail and name `Z`. Revert that edit before landing.
- Every table row's meaning matches its handler in src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts, or src/ui/tui/tui-input.ts.
- No file under src/ changes. `git diff --stat` shows only docs/cli.md, test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts, and PLANS.md.

### docs/cli.md names every long flag `tumwater help` lists, and a test keeps the two flag sets equal (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; done 2026-10-16; independent of every other Planned entry. It edits only docs/cli.md and test/cli-doc.test.ts. No source, help text, payload, or event key changes. The in-flight docs-links plan adds only test/docs-links.test.ts)

**Goal.** test/cli-doc.test.ts checks that docs/cli.md names every *command* `tumwater help` lists, but nothing compares *flags*. A prototype scan on 2026-10-16 matched `/(?<![\w-])--[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/g` over `HELP` (src/cli/help.ts) and over docs/cli.md. It found 46 distinct long flags in the help and 39 in the doc. Every doc flag is in the help, but seven help flags appear nowhere in the doc: `--branch` (`init` and `start`), `--port` (`gui`), `--follow` (`logs -f/--follow`), `--count` (`logs`), `--prompt` (`logs --role`), and `--roles` and `--config-keys` (`completion`). The reference says it lists "every `tumwater` command and the main flags it takes". After this plan it names them all, and a test fails when a flag is added to the help without the doc, or when the doc keeps a flag the help dropped.

**Approach.**
1. docs/cli.md: add the seven flags. Take each meaning from its help stanza in src/cli/help.ts:
   - "Start the team" block, `init` comment lines: add `# add --branch <name> to name the branch a new repository starts on (it seeds a new repo only)`.
   - Same block, after the `tumwater start --once` lines: add `tumwater start --branch <name>  # merge into that branch instead of baseBranch in tumwater.json or the checked-out branch; it must exist`. That is `resolveMainBranch` in src/gates/startup-gate.ts: `--branch` wins, then `config.baseBranch`, then the current branch, and an explicit name that does not exist is a startup problem.
   - The paragraph after that block that starts "`gui --all-interfaces` exposes…": put `` `tumwater gui --port N` serves the dashboard on another port than 7180; `` before it.
   - "Check state" row: change `` `tumwater logs -f` `` to `` `tumwater logs -f` (`--follow`) ``. After the `--type` item, add `` `tumwater logs --count` (one `N × <type>` line per event type present in the selected window, most frequent first; with `--json`, one object mapping type to count) ``. Change `` `tumwater logs --role <id>` `` to `` `tumwater logs --role <id> [--prompt]` (that role's pi transcript; `--prompt` also shows each run's exact prompt text) ``.
   - The closing completion paragraph: after its first sentence, add `` `tumwater completion --roles` and `tumwater completion --config-keys` print the role ids and config keys that script completes. ``
   Leave every other row unchanged.
2. test/cli-doc.test.ts: add a module-level `const LONG_FLAG = /(?<![\w-])--[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/g;` and a helper `longFlags(text: string): Set<string>` that returns `new Set(text.match(LONG_FLAG) ?? [])`. Add two tests that use the existing `DOC` and `HELP` imports:
   - "docs/cli.md names every long flag `tumwater help` lists": `missing` holds the help flags that are not in the doc's set. Run `assert.deepEqual(missing, [])`, then assert that the help set's size is at least 40 (a floor, so a regex regression cannot pass vacuously).
   - "docs/cli.md names no long flag `tumwater help` lacks": `stale` holds the doc flags that are not in the help's set. Run `assert.deepEqual(stale, [])`.
   Update the file's doc comment to say it also compares the long flags.

### Every relative link and backticked repo path in the current docs resolves, and a test keeps them that way (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry. It adds only test/docs-links.test.ts. No doc, source, payload, or event key changes) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** README.md and the current docs point readers at files in two ways: relative markdown links such as `[docs/cli.md](docs/cli.md)`, `[plans/agent-backends.md §3](plans/agent-backends.md)`, and `[backends.md](backends.md#…)`, and backticked repo paths such as `` `src/cli/help.ts` ``. Only docs/invariants.md has an existence check, and it covers only that file's register entries (`citedPaths` in test/invariants-doc.test.ts). The Plain terms code series (team, runner, run, merge, cleanup) will move whole `src/` directories, and a doc that still names the old path would go stale without anything failing. A prototype scan on 2026-10-16 found 278 links and paths. Every link, and every `#anchor` that points into a .md file, resolves. The only paths that do not resolve are in docs/glossary.md's "Code identifiers" table rows, which name the post-rename directories (`src/team/`, `src/runner/`, `src/run/`, `src/merge/`) on purpose, and the `test/...` placeholder in docs/invariants.md. So the guard lands green and catches the next stale reference.

**Approach.** `test/docs-links.test.ts` (new; modelled on test/config-doc.test.ts, with `ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../", import.meta.url))` and paths joined onto it). Export nothing.
- Docs scanned: README.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, and every `docs/*.md` (`fs.readdirSync`). Skip any file whose first five lines contain the historical banner `> Written before the 2026-10-16 plain-terms rename`, which marks the twelve dated records that stay as written. Skip lines inside fenced blocks: toggle the fence state on any line matching `/^\s*```/`.
- Links: each match of `/\]\(([^)\s]+)\)/g`. Skip targets with a scheme (`/^[a-z]+:/i`, which covers http, https, and mailto). Split the target at `#`. A non-empty path part resolves against the linking file's directory and must exist (`fs.existsSync`). When the target has a fragment and points to a `.md` file (or is `#…` alone, meaning the same file), the fragment must be one of that file's heading anchors. To build the anchors, take every `#{1,6} ` heading outside fenced blocks, trim and lowercase it, delete each character that does not match `[\p{L}\p{N}\s_-]` (with the `u` flag), and replace each whitespace character with `-`. This is GitHub's slug rule without duplicate-heading suffixes. The prototype resolved all five current anchored links with it.
- Paths: each inline code span matching `` /`((?:src|test|docs|plans|scripts)\/[\w./-]+)`/g ``, resolved against `ROOT`. Skip a match that contains `...`, which is a placeholder such as `test/...`. Skip docs/invariants.md for paths only, because test/invariants-doc.test.ts already checks them there. In docs/glossary.md, skip table rows (lines starting with `|`) for paths only: its "Code identifiers" table names directories that the Plain terms code series will create.
- Test 1: collect `"<file>:<line> <target>"` for every link, anchor, or path that does not resolve, then run one `assert.deepEqual(broken, [])` so the failure names every hit.
- Test 2, a sanity floor so that a regex or ROOT regression cannot pass vacuously: the scan checks at least one link in README.md, at least one anchored link, and at least one backticked path in DEVELOPMENT.md (65 on 2026-10-16). Collect these counts during the same scan.

**Files touched.** test/docs-links.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Test 1 passes on the tree as it lands. Temporarily changing README.md's `(docs/cli.md)` link to `(docs/cli-missing.md)` makes it fail and name `README.md:<line> docs/cli-missing.md`. Temporarily breaking the `#…` fragment of an anchored link makes it fail and name that link. Revert both edits before landing.
- Test 2 passes.
- `git diff --stat` shows only test/docs-links.test.ts and PLANS.md.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms event log, part 6/9: Write the source field and read it everywhere (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 5/9 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Event log"; touches src/events/ src/cli/notify-command.ts src/history/history-data.ts src/failure/time-spend.ts src/tick/ src/config/config-validation.ts test/) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** Stage 1 of "Widely used fields":
- Every event is written with `source`: the runner id, or `"tumwater"` for tumwater's own events, which were formerly `"harness"`.
- Every reader reads `source`.
- `HarnessEventInput` still accepts the deprecated `loop`, so call sites can switch in parts 7/9 and 8/9.

**Approach.**
- src/events/events.ts:
  - `HarnessEvent.source: string` replaces `loop`.
  - Export `TUMWATER_SOURCE = "tumwater"`.
  - `HarnessEventInput` takes exactly one of `source` or a `/** @deprecated use source */ loop`, written as a union of the two shapes beside the index signature.
  - `warnEvent` and `warnEventBestEffort` name their parameter `source`.
  - `logEventBestEffort`'s stderr fallback names `event.source ?? event.loop`.

  1. A staged-claim `claim` line also carries a payload `source: "staged"`. Move that value to `origin` first.

- Readers. tsc misses most of these because the index signature is `unknown`, so grep for `.loop` on events:

  Ignore `.loop` on objects that are not events: history rows, gui-styles.ts CSS names, and the API feed item key, which Plain terms scripting owns.
- src/events/ writers switch here: notify.ts's `warnEventBestEffort` calls. In src/cli/notify-command.ts, `NOTIFY_TEST_LOOP` becomes `NOTIFY_TEST_SOURCE = TUMWATER_SOURCE`.
- Edge: refuse a custom role named `tumwater` in src/config/config-validation.ts, because its events would be indistinguishable from tumwater's own. Name the reason in the message.
- Tests:
  - Read-back events' `.loop` becomes `.source`, and `"harness"` expectations become `"tumwater"`.
  - `HarnessEvent`-typed literals use `source`.

**Goal.** docs/config.md is the settings reference that README.md and `tumwater help` point to. Its prose names about 20 of the top-level keys in `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` (`src/config/config-schema.ts`). docs/backends.md names a few more. Keys such as `check`, `review`, `idleBackoff`, `autoRestart`, `bootstrap`, `thrashTurns`, `thrashMinutes`, `logMaxBytes`, `sessionRetentionDays`, `maxConcurrentChecks`, `baseBranch`, `piArgs` and `agentBin` appear in neither. An operator can see their values with `tumwater config`, but nothing says what they do. Nothing ties the doc to the schema either, so a key added later goes undocumented without anyone noticing. This plan adds a table with one row per top-level key and per `roles.<id>` field, plus a test that fails when a row is missing or stale.

**Approach.**
- docs/config.md: after the existing prose and before the "Model backends … are covered in backends.md" paragraph, add a `## Every setting` section. It holds two markdown tables, each with the columns `| Key | Default | What it does |`.
  1. One row per entry of `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`, in that array's order. The Key cell is exactly `` `<key>` `` (one backticked key, nothing else in the cell). The Default cell is the value `defaultConfig()` in `src/config/config.ts` sets, written as JSON (`50`, `"pi"`, `[]`), with any unit spelled out where the name does not carry it (for example `14400` for `runTimeoutSeconds`). Write `none` when `defaultConfig()` leaves the key unset. For `roles`, write "the built-in catalog" instead. The "What it does" cell is one sentence taken from that key's doc comment on `TumwaterConfig` in `src/config/config-schema.ts`. It says what the key controls and what 0 or absent means when the comment says so. Where docs/backends.md or an existing paragraph of docs/config.md already explains the key, end the cell with a link to it (for example `see [backends.md](backends.md)`) and do not restate the explanation. `fallback` and `fallbackModel` each get a row, and the `fallbackModel` row says the two keys are mutually exclusive, as the schema comment says.
  2. A `roles.<id>` table, one row per entry of `ROLE_ENTRY_KEYS`, in that order. The Key cell is `` `<field>` ``. The Default cell gives the catalog default where `defaultConfig()` sets one per role (for example, `minRunIntervalSeconds` is `3600` for plan and organize, `21600` for steward, otherwise the top-level value). It notes that `instances` above 1 is accepted only for feature and bugfix (1–8), as the existing prose says.
  Put one sentence above the tables: `tumwater config` prints the effective values, and `tumwater config get|set|unset <key>` reads or writes them. Do not edit the existing prose paragraphs.
- test/config-doc.test.ts (new; it reads the doc file the way `test/invariants-doc.test.ts` resolves `docs/invariants.md`): parse the `## Every setting` section of docs/config.md. Treat each table row whose first cell is a single backticked identifier (`/^\| `([A-Za-z]+)` \|/m`) as a documented key. Split the two tables at the `roles.<id>` heading or caption the implementer chose, and assert:
  - the first table's keys equal `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`, in order (`assert.deepEqual`), so a missing row, an extra row, a stale (renamed) row and a reordering all fail with the array diff;
  - the second table's keys equal `ROLE_ENTRY_KEYS`, in order;
  - every row has three non-empty cells.
  Add a module doc comment, as invariants-doc.test.ts has, saying why the guard exists: a key added to `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` must be documented in the same change.
- DEVELOPMENT.md: when it has a "when you add a config key" checklist (`grep -n -i "config key\|TOP_LEVEL_KEYS" DEVELOPMENT.md`), add one bullet saying to add the docs/config.md row. When it has no such checklist, leave it alone.

**Files touched.** docs/config.md, test/config-doc.test.ts (new), possibly DEVELOPMENT.md (one bullet).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- docs/config.md has a `## Every setting` section whose first table lists every `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` entry once, in array order, and whose second table lists every `ROLE_ENTRY_KEYS` entry once, in array order. Each Default cell matches `defaultConfig()`. The implementer checks the Default cells by printing `JSON.stringify(defaultConfig())` from the built `dist/` once and comparing, and reports that in VERIFIED.
- `test/config-doc.test.ts` passes on the new doc. Deleting any one row, or adding a row for a key that is not in `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`, makes it fail. Check this by hand once and report it in VERIFIED; the test itself is not required to mutate the doc.
- The existing docs/config.md prose paragraphs are unchanged (`git diff docs/config.md` shows only added lines).
- `npm run test` passes.

### The dashboard's Plans and Bugs tabs list the newest done plans and fixed bugs below the open ones, so an operator sees what the team finished lately without the CLI (planned 2026-10-16 by plan, replanned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry. It adds `finishedTitle` to `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` and edits `statusPayload` in `src/ui/status-payload.ts` and `renderBacklog` in `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts`, with tests in `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`, `test/status-payload.test.ts` and `test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`, plus one clause in `docs/cli.md`. It adds two new payload keys and renames none. The in-flight Plain terms parts edit history/run-trail keys and tick events, and none of them touches these functions; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `tumwater plan --list --done` and `tumwater bug --list --done` show the newest finished entries. The dashboard does not. Its Plans and Bugs tabs list only `## Planned` and `## Open`, so once a plan merges it disappears from the dashboard. This plan adds a short "Done recently" section under the Plans tab and a "Fixed recently" section under the Bugs tab. It follows the "Answered recently" section the Questions tab already has (the `answered` block in `renderBacklog`).

**Why this was replanned (2026-10-16).** Two review rounds rejected an implementation that cleaned finished titles in the browser with `.replace` patterns in `gui-client-fleet.ts`. Real `## Fixed` headings end in shapes those patterns missed, so the completion date showed twice, in the title and in the meta. Examples are `… now under ## Fixed); fixed 2026-10-04 by bugfix loop)` (a stray `)` after a closed parenthetical) and `… (observed 2026-10-04: … "npm"), fixed 2026-10-04 by bugfix loop)`. Done plans also end in `… test/) — done 2026-10-16`. The client-side pattern also had no test. This revision does all title cleanup server-side in one pure, unit-tested helper, and the client renders the title it receives as is.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`: beside `stripEntryStamp`, add and export `finishedTitle(title: string, dateRe: RegExp): string`. It is the heading of a `## Done`/`## Fixed` entry with its completion stamp removed. Put it in this module, not `backlog.ts`, because `backlog-structure.ts` already imports `backlog.ts` and the reverse import would form a cycle. Steps, in order:
  1. Find the FIRST match of `dateRe` (a non-global `dateRe.exec(title)`). When there is none, `t = title`. Otherwise `t = title.slice(0, match.index)`. Cutting at the first match means no completion verb plus date survives anywhere in the result.
  2. Scan `t` for unbalanced parentheses with a stack of `(` indices (pop on `)` when the stack is non-empty, and ignore a `)` on an empty stack). When the stack is non-empty at the end, cut `t` at the bottom-most unclosed `(` (`stack[0]`). This drops an open `(found by … 2026-10-01; ` or `(planned …; ` that the cut left behind.
  3. Trim trailing separators: `t = t.replace(/[\s,;:—–-]+$/, "")`.
  4. Return `stripEntryStamp(t).trimEnd()`. This drops a remaining closed `(planned …)`/`(found …)` stamp suffix, for example on an undated heading.
  Add a doc comment naming the shapes it handles, and state that `dateRe` matches nothing in its result.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: import `donePlanEntries`, `fixedBugEntries`, `completionDate`, `DONE_DATE_RE` and `FIXED_DATE_RE` from `../backlog/backlog.js`, and `finishedTitle` from `../backlog/backlog-structure.js`. Add `const DASHBOARD_RECENT_FINISHED = 5` beside `DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS` with a one-line comment (an opinionated default, no knob). Add a module-local `recentFinished(entries: BacklogEntry[], dateRe: RegExp): { title: string; completedOn: string | null }[]`. It returns `entries.slice(0, DASHBOARD_RECENT_FINISHED).map((e) => ({ title: finishedTitle(e.title, dateRe), completedOn: completionDate(e.title, dateRe) }))`. Both sections are newest first in file order (see the doc comments on `donePlanEntries` and `fixedBugEntries`). Add the payload fields `donePlans: recentFinished(donePlanEntries(root), DONE_DATE_RE)` and `fixedBugs: recentFinished(fixedBugEntries(root), FIXED_DATE_RE)` beside `answeredQuestions`, under one comment: newest first, cleaned titles only and no bodies, read fresh each poll. Badges and alerts keep counting open entries only. Change no existing key.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts` `renderBacklog`: right after the existing `answered` block, add `const finished = key === "plans" ? (d.donePlans || []) : key === "bugs" ? (d.fixedBugs || []) : [];`. When it is non-empty, append the divider `<div class='list-item list-divider'><span class='li-meta'>` + (`Done recently` for plans, `Fixed recently` for bugs) + `</span></div>`. Then append one non-interactive row per entry: `<div class='list-item t-gray'><span class='li-icon'>` + `icon("check")` + `</span><div class='li-main'><span class='li-title'>` + `esc(f.title)` + `</span>` + (f.completedOn ? `<span class='li-meta'>` + esc((key === "plans" ? "done " : "fixed ") + f.completedOn) + `</span>` : "") + `</div></div>`. Render the title exactly as received, with no `splitTitle` and no `.replace`, because the server already cleaned it. Finished rows carry no `backloglink`, no `data-index` and no button, because the drawer and edit/cancel address `## Planned`/`## Open` positions only. The block runs before the "New plan"/"File a bug" prepend and also when the open list is empty, as the answered block does. Add no new CSS.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the row documenting `plan --list --done`/`bug --list --done` (`grep -n "list --done" docs/cli.md`), add one clause saying the dashboard's Plans and Bugs tabs also list the 5 newest done plans and fixed bugs.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`, `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`, `test/status-payload.test.ts`, `test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit (`test/backlog-structure.test.ts`): `finishedTitle` maps each input to the expected output, one table-driven test:
  - `"X (planned 2026-10-01 by plan; touches src/x) — done 2026-10-03"` → `"X"` (DONE_DATE_RE)
  - `"P (planned 2026-10-01 by plan; done 2026-10-02)"` → `"P"` (DONE_DATE_RE)
  - `"Y (found by bugfix 2026-10-01) — fixed 2026-10-02"` → `"Y"`
  - `"Y2 (found by bugfix 2026-10-01; fixed 2026-10-02 by bugfix loop)"` → `"Y2"`
  - `"Z (split 2026-10-01 from W, now under ## Fixed); fixed 2026-10-04 by bugfix loop)"` → `"Z (split 2026-10-01 from W, now under ## Fixed)"` (the BUGS.md stray-`)` shape)
  - `'V (observed 2026-10-04: status read "npm"), fixed 2026-10-04 by bugfix loop)'` → `'V (observed 2026-10-04: status read "npm")'`
  - `"R (found 2026-10-01) — fixed 2026-10-02, re-landed 2026-10-05"` → `"R"`
  - `"U (planned 2026-10-01 by plan)"` (undated) → `"U"`
  - `"T with no stamp"` → `"T with no stamp"`
  The same test asserts that `dateRe` does not match any expected output.
- Repo check, reported in VERIFIED rather than added as a test: a one-off script over this repo's BUGS.md `## Fixed` and PLANS.md `## Done` headings (via `fixedBugEntries`/`donePlanEntries` from the built `dist/`) finds no `finishedTitle` result that `FIXED_DATE_RE`/`DONE_DATE_RE` matches, and no result that is empty.
- Unit (`test/status-payload.test.ts`, beside "status payload lists the five newest answered questions beside the open ones"): take a temp project whose PLANS.md has one planned entry and six done entries `D6 (planned 2026-09-30 by plan) — done 2026-10-06` … `D1 … — done 2026-10-01`, written newest first. Its BUGS.md has the fixed bugs `B2 (found by bugfix 2026-10-01; fixed 2026-10-03 by bugfix loop)` and `B1 with no stamp`. Then `donePlans` has 5 entries with titles exactly `D6`…`D2`, and the first `completedOn` is `"2026-10-06"`. `fixedBugs` equals `[{ title: "B2", completedOn: "2026-10-03" }, { title: "B1 with no stamp", completedOn: null }]`. `plans` still lists only the planned entry.
- Unit (`test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`, beside "the Questions tab lists answered questions under the open ones, read-only"): `renderBacklog` on the Plans tab with one planned title and two `donePlans` (`{ title: "A <b>x</b>", completedOn: "2026-10-05" }` and `{ title: "Old (split 2026-10-01 from W)", completedOn: null }`) paints the planned row, then the "Done recently" divider, then `A &lt;b&gt;x&lt;/b&gt;` with `done 2026-10-05`. The second title appears verbatim, parenthetical included, because the client does no stripping, and it has no meta. The finished rows contain no `backloglink` or `data-index`. The Bugs tab with `fixedBugs` shows "Fixed recently" and `fixed <date>`. With `donePlans`/`fixedBugs` absent or empty, neither divider text appears. The Questions tab never shows finished rows, and the Plans tab never shows fixed bugs.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The TUI's project-status pane lists the newest answered questions with their decisions below the open ones, so an operator in the terminal sees what was decided lately, as the dashboard's Questions tab shows (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; done 2026-10-16; independent of every other Planned entry. It edits `backlogLines` in `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`, the backlog branch of `paneBody` in `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, and exports one constant from `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, with tests in `test/tui-backlog.test.ts` plus one clause in `docs/cli.md`. It renames no payload key and touches neither `tui-keys.ts` nor the event reader, the doctor/retire/role JSON keys, or `renderBacklog`, which the in-flight plans edit)

**Goal.** The dashboard's Questions tab lists the 5 newest answered questions with their answer lines (the done entry "The dashboard's Questions tab lists the newest answered questions …"), and `tumwater questions --answered` prints them too. The TUI's project-status pane lists only `## Open` questions. Once a question is answered it disappears from the TUI, and an empty Questions section just reads `(none)`. This plan adds an `answered recently (K):` section under `open questions`. Each row shows the title and the decision preview, read-only.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: export the existing `DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS` constant (value 5, unchanged) so the TUI shows the same count. Change nothing else.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts` `backlogLines`: add an optional fifth parameter `answered: string[] = []`, placed after `planCount`. When `answered` is non-empty, append `answered recently (${answered.length}):` and then the lines. When it is empty, add nothing: no subheader and no `(none)`, so every existing call and test output stays the same. The single `(no planned features, open bugs, or open questions)` line is returned only when all four lists are empty. When the only non-empty list is `answered`, render the three open subheaders with `(none)` followed by the answered section. Update the doc comment to cover the new section.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, list-mode branch of `paneBody` (`pane.kind === "backlog"`, `sel === null`): import `answeredQuestionSummaries` from `../../backlog/question-answer.js` and `DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS` from `../status-payload.js`. Build `answeredQuestionSummaries(root, DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS).map((q) => q.decision ? `${q.title} — ${q.decision}` : q.title)`. This is the `title — decision` form `answeredQuestionList` prints. Pass the result as `backlogLines`' fifth argument. Read it only in list mode, not in entry mode. Extend the bold-subheader regex in the same `.map` from `(?:plans|open bugs|open questions)` to also match `answered recently`. Answered rows stay out of `labeledBacklogEntries`, so the selection, Ctrl+A and the edit/cancel keys still reach only the open entries, whose positions `questions answer <n>` addresses. The existing `.slice(0, eventBudget)` keeps the head, so on a short terminal the answered rows are the first lines dropped.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the "Answer open questions" row, after "the dashboard's Questions tab also lists the 5 newest answered questions with their answer lines", add that the TUI's backlog pane lists them too, read-only, under the open ones.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/tui-backlog.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit (`test/tui-backlog.test.ts`, beside "backlogLines renders subheaders with counts, entries in order"): `backlogLines(["plan A"], [], [], 1, ["Q — yes"])` ends with `"answered recently (1):", "Q — yes"`. `backlogLines([], [], [], 0, ["Q — yes"])` returns the three subheaders, each followed by `(none)`, then the answered section, and not the single "nothing" line. The existing `backlogLines` assertions pass unchanged.
- Unit (same file, beside "paneBody's backlog list and entry mode show the same eligibility mark beside the title"): take a temp project whose QUESTIONS.md has one open question and six answered ones (A1…A6 appended oldest first, each with an `**Answered 2026-10-0N by operator:** pick N` line). In list mode, `paneBody({ kind: "backlog" }, …)` shows `answered recently (5):` after the open question. The next row starts with `A6` and contains `pick 6`, and `A1` does not appear. The `answered recently (5):` row is bold, as the other subheaders are. With `selectedEntry: 1`, the pane clamps to the open question (the flat list holds only the one open entry) and does not show an answered entry. With no answered questions, the text `answered recently` does not appear.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms scripting, part 3/5: Rename the history and run-trail JSON keys and move GET /api/tick to /api/run (done 2026-10-16, planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 2/5 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Script interfaces"; touches src/history and src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts and src/gui and the dashboard History view)

**Goal.** These script-facing names change:
- `history --json` rows and `/api/history` rows carry `role` and `run`.
- The summary (`history --summary --json`, and `/api/history?summary`) has the shape `{roles: [{role, runs, changes, none, problems, tokens, costUsd, lastChangeTs}], total}`.
- The run trail (`history <role> <n> --json`) carries `run` and `merge`.
- `GET /api/tick?role=<id>&tick=N` becomes `GET /api/run?role=<id>&run=N`, and the old route is not kept.

**Approach.**
- History rows and summary (src/history/history-data.ts):
  - `TickRow.loop` → `role`, `TickRow.tick` → `run`.
  - `HistorySummaryRow.loop` → `role`, `.ticks` → `runs`.
  - `summarizeTickRows` returns `{ roles, total }`, and the total row's `role` is `"total"`.
  - The class counts (`changes`, `none`, `problems`) and `lastChangeTs` keep their names. Plain terms commands kept `HISTORY_RESULT_CLASSES` internal and maps `--result merged` to the `changes` class, so the summary's class keys and the dashboard's History filter values stay as they are.
  - `TickRowCells` holds the text table's column keys, not payload keys. Leave it.
  - Let `tsc` drive the typed readers: `renderSummary` and `renderRow` (src/history/history-render.ts), `windowSummary` (src/cli/cli-run.ts), src/ui/tui/tui-history.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts and src/tick/tick-detail.ts.
- Run trail (src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts): `TickDetail.tick` → `run`, `TickDetail.landing` → `merge`. The readers are `renderTickDetail` and `tickDetailStat` in src/tick/tick-detail.ts, and the TUI trail pane. `TickDetail.events` holds raw events, whose fields belong to Plain terms event log.
- Route:
  - In `guiRoutes` (src/gui/gui-server.ts), `"GET /api/tick"` becomes `"GET /api/run"`.
  - `handleTick` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) reads the query parameter `run` instead of `tick`, as `intQuery(q, res, "run", "positive")`. Update its doc comment and every other comment in src/gui/ that names `/api/tick`.

### Plain terms event log, part 1/9: Normalize old event lines on read and rename the fleet pause events (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires Plain terms text 19/19 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Event log"; touches src/events/ src/cli/log-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts src/gates/pause-gates.ts src/failure/failure-state-change.ts docs/cli.md test/) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** Every reader of `.tumwater/log/events.jsonl`, and of its rotated `events.jsonl.1`, sees old lines under today's names through one function, `normalizeLegacyEvent`. `tumwater logs --type` also accepts an old type name. This part maps one family, `fleet_paused`/`fleet_resumed` → `team_paused`/`team_resumed`, so every place the normalizer is wired in is tested against a real old line.

**Approach.**
- New module `src/events/event-legacy.ts`:
  - `LEGACY_EVENT_TYPES` maps an old type name to its `HarnessEvent["type"]`. This part adds `fleet_paused → team_paused` and `fleet_resumed → team_resumed`.
  - An ordered rewrite list, with entries `{ name, apply(ev) }`, starts empty. Later parts append field rewrites to it, and each rewrite runs in list order after the type rename.
  - `normalizeLegacyEvent(ev)` rewrites the freshly parsed object in place and returns it: first the type rename, then each rewrite.
    - It never throws. A field is rewritten only when it has the expected JS type, and a current line comes back untouched.
    - Per line, it costs one map lookup plus each rewrite's own guard (`history` scans ~26k lines).
  - `canonicalEventType(name)` returns the new name for an old one and any other string unchanged.
  - The module's doc comment says that role ids (`dry`, `telemetry`) are deliberately not mapped here. The Plain terms role ids series aliases an event's `source` id through its own legacy-id table when it switches each id, so mapping them here would show `dedupe` while the role is still `dry`.
  - If the vocabulary guard flags a line that holds an old name, end it with `// vocabulary-ok: legacy event name read from old logs`.
- Wire it in at the two choke points:
  - `parseEventLine` (src/events/event-read.ts) returns the normalized object. Every file read already goes through it:
    - `readEvents`/`readEventsTailWithEnd`;
    - event-window.ts's `scanEventsFile` (live log and archive) and `classifyLogText`;
    - the `followFile` callback in `cmdLogs` (`logs -f`);
    - report-data.ts's `foldLineInto` (the report fold cache's append path);
    - maintenance-quota.ts's `foldLine`.

    Grep src for any other `JSON.parse`/`parseJsonObject` of an event line and route it through `parseEventLine`.
  - `logEvent` (src/events/events.ts) normalizes the `{ ts, ...event }` object it builds before appending it and before notifying `subscribeEvents` listeners. The written line and what notify and the `run` narration receive then match what readers see. Parts 6/9–9/9 rely on this to accept the deprecated `loop` input.
- `cmdLogs` (src/cli/log-commands.ts): compare `e.type` against `canonicalEventType(type)` in the `--since` path, the `-n` path and the follow path. The empty-match prose still names the value the user typed. Add one clause to the `--type` help line in src/cli/help.ts and to docs/cli.md's `logs --type` mention: an older event name matches its current one.
- Rename the family:
  - the `HarnessEvent["type"]` union members and their comments in events.ts;
  - the writer in `pollPauseGates` (src/gates/pause-gates.ts);
  - `STATE_CHANGE_TYPES` and its switch in src/failure/failure-state-change.ts;
  - the cases in event-format.ts;
  - the keys of the groundwork's event-type label map behind `eventTypeLabel`, in both its server and browser forms.
- Tests: add test/event-legacy.test.ts, and update what typecheck or the suite flags (test/pause-gates.test.ts, test/orchestrator-pause.e2e.test.ts, test/failure-state-change.test.ts, …). Leave event lines that tests write straight to disk (`writeEvents`, `writeLogLines`, `JSON.stringify` into events.jsonl) under their old names. They now exercise the normalizer. The same rule holds for every later part of this series.
- **Self-hosting:** safe in one part. The running build writes `fleet_*` until it restarts, and the new build reads those lines as `team_*`. The old build reads no `team_*` line. The one exception is a standalone dashboard still on the old build, which shows the type raw until it restarts (display only).

**Files touched.** src/events/event-legacy.ts (new), src/events/event-read.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, src/cli/log-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, src/gates/pause-gates.ts, src/failure/failure-state-change.ts, the groundwork label-map module(s), docs/cli.md; test/event-legacy.test.ts (new), test/pause-gates.test.ts, test/orchestrator-pause.e2e.test.ts, test/failure-state-change.test.ts, test/event-format-fleet.test.ts, test/log-commands*.test.ts. Reads (does not edit): src/report/report-data.ts, src/gates/maintenance-quota.ts, src/events/event-window.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A `fleet_paused` line in events.jsonl, or in events.jsonl.1 reached through `readWindowEvents`, reads back as `team_paused` from `readEvents`, `readWindowEvents` and `parseEventLine`, and a current line is returned unchanged.
- `tumwater logs --type fleet_paused` and `--type team_paused` both print that line, and `logs --json` prints it with `"type":"team_paused"`.
- `logEvent` given an old type, through a cast, appends a line and hands subscribers an event that both carry the new type.
- The pause gate logs `team_paused`/`team_resumed`, and the failure digest still lists them as state changes.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The dashboard's Questions tab lists the newest answered questions with their decisions below the open ones, so an operator sees what they and the director decided lately without the CLI (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry. It adds one export to `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`, one payload field in `statusPayload` (`src/ui/status-payload.ts`), and a section in `renderBacklog`'s Questions branch (`src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts`), with tests in `test/question-commands.test.ts`, `test/status-payload.test.ts` and `test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`. The "Answering a question wakes the role that asked it" plan also adds an export to `question-answer.ts`, in a different place (beside `questionFilingDate`), and edits the answer handlers, not the list renderer. Plain terms text 19/19 edits assembled prompts only. Neither one touches `statusPayload` or `renderBacklog`)

**Goal.** `tumwater questions --answered` shows the newest answered questions with their answer lines. The dashboard does not. Its Questions tab lists only `## Open` (`questions: openQuestions(root)` in `statusPayload`). Once a question is answered it leaves the dashboard, and the tab says "No open questions". An operator who answered from the drawer, or who wants to see what the director decided, has to open QUESTIONS.md or a terminal. This plan adds a short "Answered recently" list under the open questions, using the same answer-line preview the CLI prints.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`: add `export function answeredQuestionSummaries(root: string, count: number): { title: string; decision: string }[]` beside `answeredQuestionPayload`. It maps `answeredQuestionsNewestFirst(root, count).entries` to `{ title: e.title, decision: answerPreview(e.body) }`. These are the same title and the same truncated `**Answered …` line `answeredQuestionList` prints, so the dashboard and the CLI cannot drift apart. Doc comment: the dashboard's compact form of the `--answered` list. It sends no bodies, so each poll stays small.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: add `const DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS = 5` with a one-line comment (opinionated default, no knob). Add the payload field `answeredQuestions: answeredQuestionSummaries(root, DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS)` beside `questions`, with a comment saying it is newest first and read fresh each poll like the other backlog lists. `alerts`, the header badge and the tab badge keep counting open questions only. Do not change `questions`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts` `renderBacklog`: when `backlogTab === "questions"` and `(d.answeredQuestions || []).length > 0`, append `<div class='list-item list-divider'><span class='li-meta'>Answered recently</span></div>` after the tab's existing html (after the open rows, or after the "No open questions" empty state). Then add one non-interactive row per entry: `<div class='list-item t-gray'><span class='li-icon'>` + `icon("check")` (`check` is in `src/ui/gui/gui-icons.ts`) + `</span><div class='li-main'><span class='li-title'>` + esc(title) + `</span>` + (decision ? `<span class='li-meta'>` + esc(decision) + `</span>` : "") + `</div></div>`. Answered rows carry no `backloglink`, no `data-index` and no Answer button, because the drawer and `/api/question-answer` address open positions only. The tab badge count stays `items.questions.length`. Reuse the existing `list-divider` class. Add no new CSS unless the row needs it.
- `docs/cli.md`'s "Answer open questions" row: add one clause saying the dashboard's Questions tab also lists the 5 newest answered questions with their answer lines.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`, `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/question-commands.test.ts`, `test/status-payload.test.ts`, `test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit (`test/question-commands.test.ts`): with three answered entries in file order A, B, C, `answeredQuestionSummaries(root, 2)` deep-equals `[{ title: "C…", decision: <C's answer line> }, { title: "B…", … }]`. An entry with no `**Answered` line gets `decision: ""`. A file with an empty `## Answered` returns `[]`.
- Unit (`test/status-payload.test.ts`): a temp project whose QUESTIONS.md has one open and six answered questions yields `answeredQuestions` with length 5, newest first. `questions` still lists only the open one.
- Unit (`test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`): `renderBacklog` on the Questions tab with `questions: []` and two `answeredQuestions` paints the "No open questions" empty state, then an "Answered recently" divider, then both titles and their decisions. The answered rows contain no `backloglink` and no Answer button. With `answeredQuestions` absent or empty, the Questions tab's html has no "Answered recently" text, so payloads from older builds render as before. The Plans tab never shows answered rows.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Answering a question wakes the role that asked it: `tumwater questions answer`, the dashboard and the TUI wake the role named in the heading's `(asked by <role> …)` clause, as `plan --release` wakes the role it hands work back to (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry)

**Goal.** A loop that hits a fork that is the user's call writes a QUESTIONS.md `## Open` entry headed `… (asked by <role> YYYY-MM-DD)`, then sleeps. When the operator answers, nothing tells that loop. The answer path (`answerQuestion`/`answerQuestionFromText` in src/cli/question-commands.ts, called by `cmdQuestions` in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts; `handleQuestionAnswer` in src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts; the answer-mode Enter branch in src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts) commits the file and never calls `requestWake`. The role that asked waits out its backoff before it reads the decision it was blocked on. `plan --release` already calls `requestWake(root, [role])` (src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts), and `submitRolePromptAndWake` (src/operator/operator-intent.ts) pairs a prompt with its wake. Answering a question is the same kind of hand-back.

**Approach.**
- src/backlog/question-answer.ts: add `export function questionAsker(title: string): string | null` beside `questionFilingDate`. It returns the first word after `asked by` in the heading's parenthetical (`/\(asked by ([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/`), or null when there is none. Doc comment: taken from the title only, like the filing date.
- src/operator/operator-intent.ts: add `export function wakeQuestionAsker(root: string, title: string): string | null`. It reads `questionAsker(title)`. When that id is in `knownRoleIdsCached(root)` (src/config/config.ts, which covers the director and instance ids like `feature-2`), it returns `requestWake(root, [asker])`. Otherwise it returns null, which covers "asked by the user", an unknown or removed role, and no clause. Never throw for an unknown asker.
- Call it after the successful commit on every answer surface:
  - `cmdQuestions` (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts), at all three answered branches (`--file`, editor, positional). In prose mode, print the wake confirmation on its own line after `sayAnswered`'s line when it is non-null. Leave the `--json` payload as it is, following the `--release` precedent of printing the wake only in prose.
  - `handleQuestionAnswer` (src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts): on `answered`, add `wake: <text>` to the 200 payload only when the result is non-null, so the payload for a question with no asker stays the same.
  - The TUI answer branch in src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts: on `answered`, append ` · woke <asker>` to the existing `answered question #N: …` flash when the wake ran. Use `questionAsker` for the name. Leave the other flash strings alone.
- docs/cli.md "Answer open questions" row: add that answering wakes the role named in the question's `(asked by …)` clause. docs/invariants.md: next to the sentence that says question answers commit as `Answer question: <title>`, add that an answer wakes a known asking role and wakes no role for an unknown or missing asker, pinned to the new test.

### An operator's own commits wake idle maintenance roles: `workLanded` counts `tumwater(operator):` subjects like human commits, so editing the brief, filing a plan or bug, or answering a question is news to a deferred role (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry)

**Goal.** The initial prompt says a sleeping loop "starts again after a while to see if the answer has changed due to the new state of the world." The user's own steering is the largest change to that world. Today it does not wake deferred maintenance roles. `tumwater brief --file`/`--edit` (src/brief/brief-edit.ts), `tumwater plan`/`bug` file/cancel/release/edit (src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts), `tumwater questions answer` (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts), and the dashboard and TUI twins (src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts) all commit to main through `commitOperatorBacklogEdit` with the subject `stampedSubject("operator", …)`, so the subject is `tumwater(operator): …`. `workLanded` in src/scheduling/scheduling.ts counts only `tumwater(feature|bugfix|director):` subjects and unstamped (human) subjects. An operator commit is neither, so `deferTickReason` keeps a `no_change` maintenance role (readme, the code-maintenance roles, steward), and bugfix in search mode, deferred with reason `"no-work"` ("deferred (no new work)" in the status table) until the 3-hour `DEFER_MAX_MS` cap, even though main moved. The operator is the human. Typing the change through the CLI instead of `git commit` should not make it count for less.

**Approach.**
- In `workLanded` (src/scheduling/scheduling.ts), add `operator` to the alternation: `/^tumwater\((feature|bugfix|director|operator)\):/`. Rewrite the function's doc comment to say that an operator commit (the `tumwater(operator):` stamp written by the CLI, TUI and dashboard backlog/brief edits) is the human's own change made through tumwater, so it counts like an unstamped human commit.
- Do not change anything else. Leave the backlog-open clause (`"backlog"` deferral), the plan role's `planDeferral`, `commitTier`/the maintenance quota in src/gates/maintenance-quota.ts, and `WorkLandedCache` (src/scheduling/work-landed-cache.ts caches the verdict per head, so it needs no change) alone. Leave the `workLanded` name too: Plain terms code merge renames it later.
- Update the prose that spells out the rule, so the docs match the code: the `DEFERRABLE_ROLES` doc comment in src/roles/roles.ts (that module is `// vocabulary: plain`, so word it with the glossary: "while no feature, bugfix, director, operator or human commit has merged into main since their last run"), the two `deferTickReason`-area comments in src/scheduling/scheduling.ts that list "feature/bugfix/director/human", the `tick_deferred` comment in src/events/events.ts, and the two bullets in docs/how-it-works.md that say a maintenance role is deferred "until feature, bugfix, director, or human work lands" and that "any feature/bugfix/director/human landing wakes" bugfix. In those two docs/how-it-works.md bullets, add that your own `tumwater brief`, `plan`, `bug` and `questions answer` edits count as human work.

### `tumwater doctor`'s refusal warning says how many planned parts wait on a refused part, so a series stuck behind a refusal is visible (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `checkRefusedEntries` in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, adds one exported function to `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, and adds tests to `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts` and `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts` plus one clause in `docs/cli.md`'s Audit row. The TUI backlog pane plan edits only `src/ui/tui/`, and Plain terms text 18/19 edits role instructions and hold-mark wording, so the tests here match the doctor's own message text, never a hold mark)

**Goal.** No role clears a **Refused** note. When the refused plan is a series part that other plans require (`requires <Series> i/n landed`), every part that requires it, directly or through a chain of parts, stays blocked until a person edits or releases the refused part. The backlog index, `plan --list` and `tumwater backlog` show those parts only as `[blocked: each waits on an earlier part]` or `[blocked: requires …]`, which looks like normal progress. `checkRefusedEntries` warns about the refused entry but does not say that a series waits on it. The warning should give that count, so the operator knows that releasing or cancelling this one entry frees N parts.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: add an exported pure function `plansWaitingOn(planned: readonly BacklogEntry[], index: number): number[]`. It returns the ascending indexes into `planned` of the entries that require `planned[index]`'s own part, directly or transitively. Matching is by `partKey` (series case-insensitive, part verbatim), the same way `entryHoldAgainst` matches. When `seriesPart(planned[index].title)` is null, return `[]`. Build the reverse edges once: for each entry with a `seriesPart`, for each `requiredParts(entry.title)` ref, record that entry index under the ref's key. Then do a breadth-first walk from the root's key with a visited set of indexes, so a dependency cycle (which `checkPlanDependencies` reports) ends the walk. Never include `index` itself. The doc comment says it is the doctor's count of a refusal's stranded dependents.
2. `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `checkRefusedEntries`: for PLANS.md entries, compute `waiting = plansWaitingOn(planned, index).length`. Bugs get 0. Then:
   - The first entry's message adds, after the `stale` clause and before `more`: `; ${waiting} planned part(s) wait on it, directly or through an earlier part`, only when `waiting > 0`.
   - Each `andMore` item adds ` [${waiting} part(s) wait on it]` when `waiting > 0`, after the existing `[prerequisites no longer planned]` suffix.
   - With no waiting parts, the message is the same as today. The ok text is unchanged. Update the doc comment to say the warning counts the parts the refusal holds.
3. `docs/cli.md`, Audit row: after "flagging one whose prerequisites are no longer planned", add ", and counting the planned parts that wait on a refused part".

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts`, `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`, `docs/cli.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test `plansWaitingOn follows requires clauses transitively and stops on a cycle`. Use entries `S, part 1/3: a`, `S, part 2/3: b (requires part 1/3 landed)`, `S, part 3/3: c (requires part 2/3 landed)`, `Other`, and `T, part 1/1: d (requires S 1/3 landed)`. Then `plansWaitingOn(planned, 0)` is `[1, 2, 4]`, `plansWaitingOn(planned, 2)` is `[]`, and `plansWaitingOn(planned, 3)` (no series part) is `[]`. A second fixture, where `X, part 1/2` and `X, part 2/2` require each other, returns `[1]` for index 0 and terminates. Before writing the requires clauses in the fixtures, confirm against `requiredParts`'s parsing that they parse, for example by asserting `requiredParts` on one of them.
- New test `checkRefusedEntries counts the planned parts that wait on a refused part`. Its PLANS.md fixture has a refused `S, part 1/3` and parts 2/3 and 3/3 that require the earlier part. The warn detail contains `; 2 planned part(s) wait on it, directly or through an earlier part`. A second refused, non-series plan in the same fixture shows up in the `(and 1 more: …)` tail with no `wait on it` suffix.
- The existing tests `checkRefusedEntries warns naming the first refused entry, the rest, and how to release it` and `checkRefusedEntries reads ok with no notes, with no files, and ignores Done and Fixed` pass unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

It edits `renderBacklogMarkdown` in `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts` and reuses `groupBlockedSeries`/`partsLabel` from `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` unchanged; the dashboard plan edits only `src/ui/`; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `tumwater backlog` (`cmdBacklog` in `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`) prints every `## Planned` entry with its full body. In this repo, more than 80 parts of the Plain terms series are blocked, each waiting on an earlier part, and together they fill thousands of lines. `plan --list` (`listAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`) and the prompt's backlog index (`collapseBlockedSeries`) already show such a series as one line through `groupBlockedSeries`. `tumwater backlog` should do the same. Each series with two or more blocked parts becomes one heading with no body, placed where the first of those parts would have been. Every other entry prints as it does today. `--json` is unchanged, so scripts still get every entry.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`: import `groupBlockedSeries` and `partsLabel` from `./backlog-structure.js` (both are already exported). Add a `renderPlannedSection(entries, holds, inProgress)` beside `renderSection`. With no `holds`, it returns `renderSection("Planned features", entries, undefined, inProgress)`, so output is identical to today. With `holds`, it builds rows `{ index: i, title: entry.title, hold: holds[i] ?? null, claimer: inProgress?.[i] ?? undefined }` and maps `groupBlockedSeries(rows)`:
   - A `row` group prints exactly what `renderSection`'s loop prints for entry `index`: the heading with `holdMark` and `inProgressMark`, a blank line, the body indented two spaces, and a blank line. Move that per-entry block into a small `renderEntry(entry, hold, runner)` helper that both functions call, so the two cannot drift.
   - A `series` group prints `### ${g.series}, ${g.rows.length} blocked parts (${partsLabel(g.rows)}) [blocked: each waits on an earlier part]`, followed by one blank line. It has no body. The wording is the same as `plan --list`'s line.
   - When at least one series group was printed, add one line after the section's entries: `_(each blocked series is one heading; \`tumwater plan --show <n>\` prints a part, \`tumwater backlog --json\` lists every entry)_`, followed by a blank line.
   - An empty `entries` still prints `_(none)_`.
2. `renderBacklogMarkdown` calls `renderPlannedSection` for the Planned section. The Open bugs and Open questions sections keep `renderSection`. Bugs are not series in practice, and `plan --list` groups only plans too.
3. `cmdBacklog` needs no change. Its view already carries `holds` and `inProgress`. `--ready` removes every held entry through `readyBacklog` before rendering, so nothing can group in that mode, and its "held entries hidden" count is unchanged.
4. Help and docs: in `src/cli/help.ts`, add one clause to the `tumwater backlog [--ready] [--json]` stanza: "a series with two or more blocked parts prints as one heading (--json still lists every entry)". Add the same clause to the `tumwater backlog` text in `docs/cli.md`'s "Check state" row.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-render.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-render.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/backlog-render.test.ts`: "renderBacklogMarkdown prints a blocked series as one heading". The plans are `[Ready, S 1/3, S 2/3, S 3/3, Other]`, with holds `[null, null, {blockedBy:["S 1/3"]}, {blockedBy:["S 2/3"]}, null]`. Assert that the output holds the full headings and bodies for Ready, `S, part 1/3`, and Other; holds `### S, 2 blocked parts (2/3–3/3) [blocked: each waits on an earlier part]` once, after part 1/3's body and before Other; leaves out the bodies of parts 2/3 and 3/3; and ends the section with the `_(each blocked series is one heading; …)_` line.
- The same test checks that a part named by `inProgress` stays a full entry carrying its `[working on it: …]` mark. A lone blocked part, and a series whose second part is `"refused"`, also keep full entries, and with no series grouped there is no footer line.
- `renderBacklogMarkdown(payload)` with no `holds` returns the same string as before this change. The existing "no holds leaves the document unchanged" test still passes.
- New CLI test: `tumwater backlog` on a repo whose PLANS.md has a three-part series with parts 2 and 3 waiting on earlier parts prints the series heading once. `tumwater backlog --json` on the same repo still lists all three parts in `plans`, with `holds.plans` parallel to them.
- The existing tests in `test/backlog-render.test.ts` pass unchanged. Their fixtures have no series with two blocked parts.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The dashboard's Plans and Bugs tabs list the entries a role can pick first and gather blocked ones under a "Blocked (N)" divider, so the few ready plans are not buried among 100+ blocked parts (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `statusPayload` in `src/ui/status-payload.ts` and `renderBacklog` in `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts`, with tests in `test/status-payload.test.ts` and `test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`. The `plan --list` grouping plan edits `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` and `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, `questions --answered` edits `cmdQuestions` and `question-answer.ts`, and Plain terms text 7/19 rewords backlog command output and the role page; none touches these files. The TUI's backlog list is left alone, because Plain terms text 9/19 owns the TUI tabs and the tui-panes split is refused; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The dashboard's Plans tab paints `## Planned` in file order. Here that is well over 100 rows. The refused tui-panes plan comes first, then text 7/19, then about 100 blocked Plain terms parts, and the newest plans that roles can pick sit at the very bottom. Each row already shows its hold mark (`planHolds`), but an operator still has to scroll past every blocked row to find the plans that will run next. Show the rows a role can pick first, then the blocked rows under one divider. Every row keeps its click address.

**Approach.**
1. `src/ui/status-payload.ts` `statusPayload`: add two boolean arrays beside `planHolds`/`bugHolds`. Name them `planBlocked` and `bugBlocked`, built as `backlogHolds(root).plans.map((h) => h !== null)` (and the same for `.bugs`). Import `backlogHolds` from `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`; it is stat-cached, so the second read beside `backlogMarks` costs a cache hit. They are index-for-index parallel to `plans`/`bugs`, like `planHolds`. Any non-null `EntryHold` counts as blocked: refused, needs review, needs replan, or requires a part. An entry someone is working on but that has no hold stays `false`, so it keeps its `[working on it: …]` mark in the top group. Do not read the mark string to decide this; the Plain terms parts reword those marks.
2. `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts` `renderBacklog`, in the Plans/Bugs branch (not Questions, not the Inbox): read `blocked = key === "plans" ? (d.planBlocked || []) : key === "bugs" ? (d.bugBlocked || []) : []`. Build the row HTML for each index `i` exactly as today, then split it into two lists: rows where `blocked[i]` is false, then rows where it is true, each in file order. When the second list is not empty, put one divider row between the lists: `<div class='list-item list-divider'><span class='li-meta'>Blocked (N)</span></div>`. "Blocked" is the docs/glossary.md word for a held backlog entry. Each row keeps `data-index='i'`, its original position, so the drawer, the Answer button, and the `openEntryKey` highlight still address the right entry. When no row is blocked, or the payload has no `planBlocked`/`bugBlocked` (an older server), the HTML is the same as before. The New plan/File a bug row stays first. The tab badge still counts every entry.
3. `src/ui/gui/gui-styles.ts`: add one rule, `.list-divider { padding: 6px 16px; background: var(--surface-2); }`, plus `.list-divider:hover` holding the same background so the divider does not light up like a row.
4. No toggle and no setting. Ordering by pickability is the one default, which follows the "opinionated defaults" principle. Grouping a series into one row, as `plan --list` will, is left for a later plan once `groupBlockedSeries` lands.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-fleet.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-styles.ts`, `test/status-payload.test.ts`, `test/gui-client-fleet.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/status-payload.test.ts`: the existing "status payload carries planHolds and bugHolds parallel to plans and bugs" fixture also asserts `planBlocked` is `[false, true, true, false]` and `bugBlocked` is `[false, true]`. The working-on-it test asserts a claimed plan with no hold has `planBlocked` `false`.

In the painted HTML, B's row comes before D's, D's before the `Blocked (2)` divider, and the divider before A, then C. A's button still carries `data-index='0'` and C's carries `data-index='2'`.
- The same file adds a Bugs-tab case with one blocked bug, checking the `Blocked (1)` divider follows the pickable bug.
- "an eligible Plans row is byte-identical whether or not the payload carries holds" still passes. A new assertion in it shows that `planBlocked: [false]` paints the same HTML as a payload without the key.

- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater plan --list` shows each blocked series as one line, as the prompt's backlog index does, so an operator's list of 100+ planned entries fits on a screen and the eligible plans stand out (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other eligible Planned entry. It edits `collapseBlockedSeries` and its helpers in `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`, the plans branch of `listAndAnnounce` in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, the `plan --list` stanza of `src/cli/help.ts`, and the `--list` clause of `docs/cli.md`'s "Steer the project" row. Plain terms text 7/19, in flight, rewords messages in these two backlog files; this plan adds a grouping helper and one list branch and rewords none of the existing messages. The `questions --answered` plan edits `cmdQuestions` and `question-answer.ts` instead) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `tumwater plan --list` prints every `## Planned` entry on its own numbered line. Today that is well over 100 lines, and most are blocked parts of the Plain terms series. The prompt's `<backlog-index>` already groups those parts into one line per series (`collapseBlockedSeries`, from "Compact backlog index, part 1/1"). The operator's list should group them the same way. Numbering is unchanged: a grouped line names the positions it covers, so `--show <n>`, `--edit <n>` and `--cancel <n>` still reach every part.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`: split the grouping out of `collapseBlockedSeries` into an exported pure function, `groupBlockedSeries<T extends SeriesRow>(rows: readonly T[]): SeriesGroup<T>[]`.
   - Types: `SeriesRow = { title: string; hold: EntryHold; claimer: string | undefined }` and `SeriesGroup<T> = { kind: "row"; row: T } | { kind: "series"; series: string; rows: T[] }`.
   - Same rules as today: a row is collapsible through `collapsibleSeriesPart`, a series groups only with two or more collapsible parts, and the group sits at its first part's place.
   - Make `IndexRow` extend `SeriesRow`. Widen `collapsibleSeriesPart` and `partsLabel` to take `SeriesRow`, and export `partsLabel`.
   - Rewrite `collapseBlockedSeries` as a map over `groupBlockedSeries`. Its output stays character-for-character the same; the existing `renderBacklogIndexBlock` collapse tests in `test/backlog-structure.test.ts` pin this.
2. `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` `listAndAnnounce`: only the plan prose branch changes. That means not `bugSection`, not `--json`, and not `--done`.
   - Build one row per entry: `{ position: i + 1, title, hold: entryHolds[i] ?? null, claimer: entryRunners[i] ?? undefined }`, then call `groupBlockedSeries`.
   - A `row` group renders exactly as today: `${position}. ${title}${holdMark}${inProgressMark}${entryAgeSuffix}`.
   - A `series` group renders as `${positions}. ${series}, ${k} blocked parts (${partsLabel(rows)}) [blocked: each waits on an earlier part]`. Here `positions` joins runs of consecutive positions with an en dash (`13–17`) and separates runs with commas (`13–15, 18`).
   - Since lines are no longer numbered by index, build them directly instead of through `numberedList`. Keep the `plans in PLANS.md:` header.
   - When at least one series grouped, append one footer line: `(each blocked series is one line; --show <n> prints a part, --json lists every entry)`.
   - The `bug --list` prose, every `--json` payload, and `--done` stay unchanged.
3. `src/cli/help.ts`: add one clause to the `plan --list` stanza: "a series' blocked parts show as one line naming their positions". `docs/cli.md`: add the same clause to the `--list` sentence of the "Steer the project" row.
4. No new flag. `--json` and `--show <n>` already give every part. This follows the "opinionated defaults" principle.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`, `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`: a new test calls `groupBlockedSeries` directly on a list with:
  - an eligible part 1/4 and three blocked parts 2/4–4/4 of one series;
  - a lone blocked part of another series;
